Core primary maths practice

Fractions. Equal parts, connected ideas.

Begin with equal parts of a shape or set. Connect these pictures to numbers, equivalents and increasingly demanding calculations.

Try the practice

Build the skill in steps

  • Years 1–2: halves, quarters, thirds and quantities
  • Year 3: tenths, equivalents and same-denominator calculations
  • Years 4–5: decimal connections, related denominators and mixed numbers
  • Year 6: unlike denominators, multiplication, division and percentages

Coach can return to supporting facts when a learner needs them. Independent answers, supported answers and later-day recall remain distinct in the learning record.

Worked example

2/3 + 1/4

  1. 1Use a common denominator: 12.
  2. 22/3 = 8/12 and 1/4 = 3/12.
  3. 38/12 + 3/12 = 11/12.

Keep the method connected to meaning

Use objects, pictures or a place-value model alongside the screen when helpful. Ask the learner to explain what each step means, then give a similar question without showing the example. An answer copied from working is useful practice, but does not show independent recall.

The academy revisits earlier material after gaps and keeps practical observations separate from digital practice. Work with a teacher or grown-up when a method is unfamiliar; the resource supplements that teaching.
